title: VIP: Visual-guided Prompt Evolution for Efficient Dense Vision-Language Inference
claim: Prior approaches leave image-text activation flawed or collapsed despite refined affinity; ours also refines image-text activation.
layout: 2x2 grid of panels, arrows linking rows, dashed dividers, status icons
description: A 2x2 grid of panels, each showing a bus image rendered as heatmaps in two rows of three images. The top row of each panel is image affinity, with a red query dot. The bottom row is image-text activation for the labels {sky}, {bus} and {road}. Panel (a) CLIP solution has an orange background and a warning icon for flawed affinity. Panel (b) adds modulation on a purple background: affinity is refined with a green check, but image-text activation collapses, marked with a red cross. Panel (c) dino.txt has a teal background with refined affinity, but dotted white outlines mark mismatched regions. Panel (d) is the VIP (Ours) panel with a blue background. It uses expanded alias prompts such as {bus,...,red bus}, and both rows get green checks. Orange and green arrows link the rows, and a green double-chevron labelled 'Spatial Awareness' joins the CLIP and dino.txt halves.
caption: Comparison of image affinity and dense image-text activation. (a) Prevalent CLIP-based one-layer attention modulation methods. (b) Extended two-layers modulation on CLIP-based methods to further rectify spatial bias. (c) Spatially-aware dino.txt solution. (d) Ours \VIP, building upon dino.txt.
abstract: Pursuing training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation in an efficient and generalizable manner remains challenging due to the deep-seated spatial bias in CLIP. To overcome the limitations of existing solutions, this work moves beyond the CLIP-based paradigm and harnesses the recent spatially-aware dino$.$txt framework to facilitate more efficient and high-quality dense prediction. While dino$.$txt exhibits robust spatial awareness, we find that the semantic ambiguity of text queries gives rise to severe mismatch within its dense cross-modal interactions. To address this, we introduce Visual-guided Prompt evolution (VIP) to rectify the semantic expressiveness of text queries in dino$.$txt, unleashing its potential for fine-grained object perception. Towards this end, VIP integrates alias expansion with a visual-guided distillation mechanism to mine valuable semantic cues, which are robustly aggregated in a saliency-aware manner to yield a high-fidelity prediction. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that VIP: 1. surpasses the top-leading methods by 1.4%-8.4% average mIoU, 2. generalizes well to diverse challenging domains, and 3. requires marginal inference time and memory overhead.
